version: GA (docs page updated 2026-10-15); voice agents and agent guardrails in preview

facts.claim: Agent guardrails are in preview; four intervention points: user input, tool call (Preview), tool response (Preview), output; agent action is 'Annotate and block' only.
facts.label: from-official-docs

facts.claim: The agent's guardrail fully overrides the model's guardrail; an agent only uses Microsoft.DefaultV2 if its model deployment does or it is explicitly assigned.
facts.label: from-official-docs

D01.rationale: Content-safety guardrails with tool-call and tool-response intervention points exist but are Preview for agents; MCP tool-approval documentation could not be fetched (404), so human-approval defaults are unverified.

facts.claim: Hosted agents: each session runs in a VM-isolated sandbox connected to your VNet (BYO VNet).
facts.label: from-official-docs

D02.rationale: Hosted agents run each session in a VM-isolated sandbox; prompt agents are fully managed; code interpreter tool available.

facts.claim: Hosted agents support network egress controls (preview) configured in the same guardrail (RAI policy).
facts.label: from-official-docs

facts.claim: Private networking is available for prompt agents; hosted agents support BYO Azure VNet.
facts.label: from-official-docs

D03.rationale: Private networking for prompt agents and BYO VNet for hosted agents; network egress controls for hosted agents configured in guardrails (Preview).

facts.claim: Toolboxes expose curated tools behind one managed MCP-compatible endpoint with centralized authentication, governance and versioning.
facts.label: from-official-docs

facts.claim: Supported MCP authentication options include key-based, Entra (agent or project managed identity), OAuth identity passthrough (OBO) and unauthenticated access.
facts.label: from-official-docs

D05.rationale: Toolboxes curate tools behind one managed MCP endpoint with centralized auth, governance and versioning; MCP auth options include key, Entra agent identity, OAuth OBO and unauthenticated 'where appropriate'.

facts.claim: Blueprint federated credential (managed identity) recommended for production; no secret stored in the blueprint; some tool configs still expose the project managed identity.
facts.label: from-official-docs

facts.claim: Currently only MCP and A2A tools support agent identity authentication.
facts.label: from-official-docs

D07.rationale: Entra agent identity with federated credential from project managed identity avoids stored secrets; however only MCP and A2A tools support agent identity auth, and key-based auth remains available.

facts.claim: Built-in tools include web search, file search, code interpreter and memory.
facts.label: from-official-docs

D09.rationale: Memory is listed as a built-in tool; controls not verified.

facts.claim: All unpublished agents in a project share a common identity; docs say to treat it as a broader blast radius and publish for a distinct identity.
facts.label: from-official-docs

D10.rationale: Unpublished agents in a project share one agent identity (broader blast radius); publishing creates a distinct identity requiring manual re-assignment of RBAC roles.

facts.claim: Observability: end-to-end tracing, metrics, evaluations, Application Insights integration.
facts.label: from-official-docs

D11.rationale: End-to-end tracing, metrics, evaluations and Application Insights; Entra admin center inventories agent identities.

facts.claim: Customers can use their own Azure resources (storage, Azure AI Search, Cosmos DB) for conversation state.
facts.label: from-official-docs

D12.rationale: Not verified; bring-your-own storage/Cosmos DB/AI Search for conversation state is supported.

facts.claim: Entra admin center Agent ID: Conditional Access, identity protection, network access, governance for agent identities; blueprint lets admins disable/revoke all agents of a class.
facts.label: from-official-docs

D14.rationale: Entra Agent ID gives Conditional Access, identity protection, network access control and governance (owners/sponsors/expiry) per agent and per blueprint class, plus Azure RBAC.

facts.claim: CVE-2026-35435: Azure AI Foundry (M365 published agents) improper access control / elevation of privilege, CVSS 8.6, published 2026-05-07, server-side fix.
facts.label: third-party-report

D15.rationale: Microsoft issues CVEs via MSRC; CVE-2026-35435 (Azure AI Foundry published agents, improper access control) reported by secondary sources only (NVD/MSRC pages not retrievable).
